trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: The Fed is raising rates again (3.75-4.00% after a September 2026 hike, markets pricing a peak near 4.75% in 2027) and the 10-year Treasury is at 5.1%, so mortgages (rates the FOMC minutes call elevated), car loans, credit cards and business credit stay expensive well into the period.

trends.trend: Sticky inflation and cost of living
trends.why_it_shapes_daily_life: PCE inflation is running 3.7% in 2026 on energy, tariffs and AI-related goods prices; the Fed staff does not see 2% until 2029, so real pay, rents and grocery and fuel bills are a live grievance for years.

AI capex is the main prop under growth and stock prices and is now financed with debt ($680bn issued Jan-Oct 2026); whether it keeps running or reverses decides jobs in construction and tech, retirement account values and credit availability.

Official baselines show 2-2.4% growth and 4.1% unemployment through 2029, while prediction markets put about 20-30% on a recession by 2027 and hiring is unusually slow; the gap between baseline and tail is what people will live through.

Federal debt is projected to rise from about 100% to 120% of GDP by 2036 (CBO February 2026 baseline as reported in secondary sources; primary not obtained) and investors are demanding a higher term premium, which raises every long-term borrowing rate and squeezes room for tax cuts or benefits.

latest_edition.title: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates and Par Real Yield Curve Rates, reading for 17 November 2026

accuracy.why: About $30tn of marketable debt is repriced daily by dealers, funds and foreign reserve managers who lose money if wrong (T1, T2); tenors bind to 30 years (T4); the price is marked daily and forward-rate/breakeven forecast errors are a long-studied record (T3). Capped at 4 because forwards are biased predictors: they embed a time-varying term premium (the Nov 2026 FSR says the estimated term premium is "notably above its historical median") and TIPS breakevens embed liquidity and inflation-risk premia.

richness.why: Fourteen nominal and five real tenors per day plus three breakeven series; exact, dated numbers (mortgage and corporate borrowing costs key off them) but no entities, places or narrative.

ai.why: Reading dated 17 Nov 2026. A continuously updated price: the 10-year real yield rose from 1.94% (2 Jan 2026) to 2.89% while the 10-year breakeven stayed near 2.2%, the pattern Chow-Halperin-Mazlish associate with markets pricing faster AI-driven growth, but the files cannot separate AI from energy, fiscal supply and Fed hikes.

ai_evidence.search_note: Pure data files (CSV): no text to search. AI enters only implicitly through real yields; the FOMC minutes (see fomc-sep-minutes) attribute part of the 2026 rise in term premiums to AI-infrastructure debt issuance.

sources.why_top_or_not: Highest accuracy-conditions score in the area and the only source whose instrument tenor actually spans 2026-2036; it anchors every rate a household or firm will pay.
